Convert a detset to the tables of the trackyverse ATO

Source: R/to_ato.R
to_ato.Rd

Returns the detset as the four ATO tables, det, dep, tag and ani. Each table carries every column of ATO's own template for it (ATO 0.0.0.9006, R/ATO_class.R), in the template's order, then the mandatory tz column set to "UTC", then the detqc columns ATO does not name, as ATO allows. Template columns detqc has no value for are NA, and valid is TRUE. The mapping: animal_id becomes animal in ani and tag; station_id becomes deploy_location; tag_model, tag_serial and tag_life_days become model, serial and battery_life; and the delay range becomes ping_rate, the midpoint, and ping_variation, the half-width. sensor_unit moves from the detections to tag. ATO reads power_level as a number: a power level given as text, such as "H", is NA there, with a warning, and is kept as text in the extra column power_level_text of tag, present only when such a value exists. In det, ATO creates animal itself when it matches detections to tags, so the detection's own animal stays in the extra column animal_id. release_location in ani names the release site by its position, "R1", "R2" and so on, as to_actel() names them; it is NA for an animal with no release position.

Usage

to_ato(x, as = c("tables", "ATO"))

Arguments

x

A detset.

as

"tables" for a list of data frames. "ATO" stops, as above.

Value

A list of the data frames det, dep, tag and ani, with the attributes open_deployments and deployments.

Details

as = "ATO", which would build ATO's S4 object, stops: detqc does not build that object. Build it from these tables with ATO's make_ani(), make_dep(), make_det(), make_tag() and init_ato().

Deployments. ATO requires a recovery time, and a deployment that ends before it starts or overlaps the next one of its receiver is not a deployment ATO can read. So a deployment still in the water ends at the next deployment of its receiver, or, when there is none, one second after the last detection in the set, so that the last detection falls inside it under the contract's half-open rule. A deployment that runs past the next deployment of its receiver ends where that one starts, as detset() gives the overlap to the later one. Only the deployments that overlap the detections, from the first to the last, are exported. The attribute open_deployments counts the open deployments, and deployments counts each kind; a warning gives the counts when a deployment was trimmed or left out. to_actel() uses the same rule. No detection is removed.

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
ato_tables <- to_ato(dets)
names(ato_tables)
#> [1] "det" "dep" "tag" "ani"
head(ato_tables$det)
